hypothesis: Large language models (LLMs) have shown potential in enhancing drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction by leveraging their ability to process and generate complex language patterns, which can be applied to the interpretation of biological data [2504.05496:10]. The integration of LLMs with deep learning architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), has improved the prediction of drug-target binding affinities by using sequence information of both drugs and targets, outperforming traditional methods like KronRLS and SimBoost [deepdta:0]. LLMs can also facilitate the automation of hypothesis generation in scientific research, which could be applied to DTI prediction to identify novel interactions and repurpose existing drugs [2504.05496:9]. Furthermore, the robustness of LLMs in handling diverse data types and their ability to generalize across tasks can enhance the accuracy and efficiency of DTI predictions [centaur:102]. However, challenges such as the need for high computational resources and the risk of factual inaccuracies remain, necessitating further research to optimize LLMs for reliable DTI prediction [2504.05496:9].
